doc.title: Charles Calello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 21, 2025

title: Conducting his own sessions and missing credit
summary: He conducted all his own sessions, though the artist took arranging credit on All By Myself.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: That’s a great statement. Did you start to write – I’m going to re-phrase. When you first started to write did you need to be at the sessions so that if things went awry or a note needed to be fixed you were there for it. And then to make it a point where you didn’t have to be there anymore.

I wrote – all the arrangements I wrote I conducted on the session. I never wrote for anyone to go into – well maybe once or twice that may have happened but it wasn’t a primary thing in my career. There were times I wrote arrangements that I didn’t get credit for which – and one was “All By Myself.” The artist took the credit for the arrangement and when the musicians in the band were looking for the score they knew who to call.
